title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: A Guide for NSW Health Salary Sacrifice Considerations
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary with our 38-hour week guide. Includes NSW health salary sacrifice insights, tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: Annual pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks, assuming a standard full-time week.

faqs.q: What is the formula for converting an hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives a gross annual figure before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The result assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual estimate?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. When using the timesheet, you can tick a box to add 25% casual loading to your base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The calculator then applies the loading before multiplying by hours and weeks. For example, a base rate of $26.44 becomes $33.05 per hour with casual loading, as per the National Minimum Wage casual rate from 1 July 2026.

faqs.q: Does the calculator account for NSW health salary sacrifice?
faqs.a: No. The calculator provides an estimate of gross annual pay, tax, and super without any salary sacrifice arrangements. For NSW Health employees, salary sacrifice can reduce your taxable income by directing part of your pre-tax salary towards benefits such as a car, super contributions, or other items. This is not deducted in the estimate. You should consult your employer or a tax professional to understand how salary sacrifice affects your take-home pay. The keyword 'nsw health salary sacrifice' is relevant when considering adjustments beyond this basic calculation.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Annual Pay Formula

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to convert it to an annual figure. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for comparing offers and understanding your potential earnings.

### The Fortnightly View

Many Australian employees are paid fortnightly. To estimate your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## Key Pay Concepts in Australia

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher. If you are covered by an award, your minimum hourly rate will be specified in that award. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave). The casual minimum wage from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour. When using [the timesheet](/), you can tick a box to add 25% casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator applies it correctly.

### Superannuation

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base for super guarantee is $270,830 per year (2026–27). Earnings above that do not attract compulsory super. Our estimate calculates super at 12% of ordinary earnings up to that cap.

## Tax and Medicare

Resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. The estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

## Average Earnings and Industry Benchmarks

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. For all employees (including part-time), total earnings average $1,579.20 per week. In New South Wales, full-time ordinary time earnings are $2,108.80 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job. If you are comparing your offer, remember that your role may differ from the average.

## NSW Health Salary Sacrifice

For employees in NSW Health, salary sacrifice arrangements are common. You can sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary towards benefits such as a car, additional super contributions, or other approved items. This reduces your taxable income and can increase your take-home pay. However, the annual pay estimate on this site does not include salary sacrifice. It assumes you receive your full hourly rate as cash wages. When considering a NSW Health role, factor in any salary sacrifice options separately. The keyword 'nsw health salary sacrifice' is important for understanding your net pay.

## Using the Timesheet

The [timesheet](/) is the home page where you enter your base hourly rate. You can then see your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. The calculator assumes a 38-hour week unless you change the hours. It uses the 2026–27 tax scale and the 12% super guarantee rate. Remember that this is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

For more detailed pay guides, visit [pay guides](/blog). For reference tables on minimum wages and award rates, see [reference tables](/data). To learn about super and packaging, go to [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
